title: Decisions, markets and the circular flow
subtitle: Engineers choose between alternatives with limited money. Economics supplies the language: scarcity, demand, supply and the flow of income.

sections.title: Scarcity and the economic decision
sections.body: Resources (money, time, materials) are limited while wants are not: that is scarcity. Every choice has an opportunity cost — the value of the best alternative given up. Engineering economics compares the monetary consequences of technical alternatives so that the option giving the most benefit per unit of resource is chosen.

worked.why: You can spend Rs 100,000 on machine A (return Rs 12,000/yr) or machine B (return Rs 15,000/yr).
Choosing A gives up B’s extra return. Opportunity cost of A per year:

choices.text: The value of the best alternative forgone.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: What you give up by choosing.

sections.title: The decision process
sections.body: A rational engineering decision follows steps: define the problem, list alternatives (including “do nothing”), estimate cash flows, choose a criterion (present worth, IRR …), compare, consider non-monetary factors, decide, and review the result afterwards.

questions.prompt: Which alternative must always be considered?

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: It is the baseline for comparison.

figures.caption: Figure 1.2.1 — decision process
figures.note: The last arrow closes the loop.

sections.title: Demand and supply
sections.body: The law of demand: as price rises, quantity demanded falls. The law of supply: as price rises, quantity supplied rises. Where the curves cross is the equilibrium: price and quantity at which the market clears. If the price is above equilibrium there is a surplus and sellers cut prices; below it, a shortage and prices rise.

sections.title: Elasticity
sections.body: Price elasticity of demand E = (%ΔQ)/(%ΔP). |E| > 1: elastic (quantity reacts strongly — luxuries, substitutes available); |E| < 1: inelastic (necessities). A firm facing elastic demand raises revenue by cutting price; with inelastic demand, by raising it.

worked.why: Price rises from 20 to 22 (+10 %); quantity falls from 100 to 85 (−15 %).

sections.title: National income and the circular flow
sections.body: Households supply labour and buy goods; firms hire labour and sell goods; money flows round. GDP = the market value of final goods and services produced in a country in a year; three equal ways to measure it: production (value added), income (wages + profit + rent + interest) and expenditure: GDP = C + I + G + (X − M).

sections.title: Inflation, growth and real values
sections.body: Inflation is a general rise in prices. Real GDP divides nominal GDP by a price index to remove it. A nominal interest rate i relates to the real rate r and inflation f by (1 + i) = (1 + r)(1 + f). Ignoring inflation makes future money look bigger than it is.
